data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2019 were GBP 31.399m (2018 column). During 2019 the syndicate reported releases on prior years, with the managing agent stating that the syndicate "benefitted from GBP 2.3 million of releases on prior year catastrophe events including the California Wildfires and Superstorm Sandy." The movement is described as a prior-year release (favourable development), driven by lower-than-expected outcomes on earlier catastrophe exposures and general favourable prior-year claims development. No gross prior-year movement breakdown by individual event or LOB is provided in the notes for Syndicate 557.
raw_causal_phrases: benefitted from GBP 2.3 million of releases on prior year catastrophe events including the California Wildfires and Superstorm Sandy.
lack of significant catastrophe events impacting its mix during the year with losses from Hurricane Dorian remaining within the Syndicate's planned catastrophe expectations.
data.data_quality_notes: Opening reserves taken from Balance Sheet liabilities 'Claims outstanding' 2018 comparative column (31,399 GBP '000 = 31.399m) - high confidence. Prior year development: the report text explicitly cites a GBP 2.3m release on prior year catastrophe events; the report does not state clearly whether this GBP 2.3m is a gross (insurance liabilities) or net (after reinsurance) figure. Per rules a gross figure was preferred but not explicitly available; therefore the GBP 2.3m prior-year movement has been recorded as a release (negative) but with moderate confidence and flagged here as potentially net-of-reinsurance. A gross claims development triangle is present in the notes (claims development tables) but was not used to compute an alternative total due to readability limits in the source images; triangle data is available on page 58 but was not relied on for the prior-year movement number above. Users should treat the prior_year_development_gbp_m as an inferred release from narrative rather than a reconciled gross movements table.
